ANASTOMOSIS.MD · THE SHORTLIST · 23 OCT 2026

Anastomosis logo shortlist

Every mark that made the cut: the founder's picks, the wild wave, and the second batch — fifteen icons and eight studies of the fourth — each born inside the profile view, each one a joining-mechanism wearing the brand's blood. One name underneath them all.

THE FOUNDER’S PICKS · WHERE WE STAND

Three marks lead.

The designer's cut, the wordmark, and the emblem you picked from the wild.

DC-1

The self-tying vessel

One continuous tube: artery in through the golden ring, vein out — the infinity performing the anastomosis.

DC-2

The name carries the loop

The wordmark lockup: the two O's of anastOmosis are the infinity's loops — the name performing its own meaning.

IG-1

The emblem, in the wild

The founder's pick from the first profile-view round — the vessel-join loop as the avatar.

THE WILD WAVE · SIX JOINS, SIX ICONS

The first six.

Joining-mechanisms turned icons: crossing, ligature, embrace, seam, bridge, dovetail.

WLD-1

The crossing

Two vessels crossing at the centre, one gold suture ring, four open mouths — the surgical diagram become icon.

WLD-2

The ligature

A and M sharing one stroke — a ligature in the true typographic sense: two letters anastomosed into one glyph.

WLD-3

The embrace

Two S-curves completing one circle — the arterial and venous halves of one circulation.

WLD-4

The seam

Crimson teeth interlocking petrol teeth — the mechanical anastomosis, one gold hand-stitch at the centre.

WLD-5

The bridge

Two vertical vessels joined by a horizontal graft — the letter H as the bypass surgeons build.

WLD-6

The dovetail A

The initial split by a carpenter's dovetail seam — the mechanic's truth wearing the surgeon's letter.

THE SECOND BATCH · JOINING-MECHANISMS, ROUND TWO

Six more.

Keystone, junction, coupling, braid, confluence, splice — every one an avatar, every one the name.

WLD-7

The keystone

Two arch halves locked by one gold keystone — the arch stands only because the join holds.

WLD-8

The junction

Two tracks merging into one — the railroad anastomosis, gold pin at the switch.

WLD-9

The coupling

Two open tubes clasped mouth-to-mouth — the plumbing of the body as one fitting.

WLD-10

The braid

Two vessels woven over and under — the oldest join humans know, bound in gold.

WLD-11

The confluence

Four vessels meeting at one golden node — the medical plus sign, drawn by circulation itself.

WLD-12

The splice

Two ropes, six strands interwoven — the sailor's end-to-end anastomosis.

THE FOURTH MARK, EXPLORED · WLD-1 THE CROSSING

The crossing, eight ways.

Your pick, deep-dived: style studies for the vessels — atlas, calligraphic, woven, pure with no gold, monumental, branched, twisted, wide-mouthed.

CR-1

Atlas style

Double-contour vessels — the wall drawn like the anatomical atlases, gold ring at the crossing.

CR-2

Calligraphic

Strokes that swell and taper like a master’s brush, gold ring at the crossing.

CR-3

The weave — no gold

The crimson vessel passes over the petrol with a clean gap — the join told purely by the pass, no gold at all.

CR-4

Pure — no gold

The exact mark with the golden part removed: only the two vessels and the bone between them.

CR-5

Monumental

Ultra-thick flat bars, no lumens, no gold — the 16-pixel favicon cut.

CR-6

Branched

One small side-branch per arm — four branches, the anatomical telling, gold ring kept.

CR-7

Ribbon twist

Flat ribbons half-twisting through the crossing — the vessel’s rotation made visible, gold ring kept.

CR-8

Wide-mouthed

Generous flared lumens at all four ends — the strongest possible vessel cue, gold ring kept.
